title: Tenant fingerprint & fleet-shaping galaxy harness for throughput certification
creator: Marcus Li
description:
Build a tenant-aware throughput measurement harness (the 'Galaxy' harness) and an associated benchmarking methodology to produce reproducible
throughput guarantees for Dedicated customers. The harness must validate tail and steady-state
SLOs, exercise autoscaler policies end-to-end, and surface fleet-level shaping/fallback behavior
that affects customer-facing latency and capacity. Deliverables: harness code, operator runbook,
customer acceptance checklist, and a set of validated golden-run signatures for common tenant mixes.
background:
Customers buying Dedicated capacity expect predictable throughput under their tenant mixes and
autoscale behaviors. Existing load suites focus on single-tenant ramp-and-sustain profiles; they do not
capture realistic tenant mixing, admission-control shaping, autoscaler hysteresis, or KV-cache warmup
effects that materially change per-tenant throughput guarantees. This ticket scopes a harness that
closes that gap and feeds Customer Acceptance Tests (CATs) used during onboarding.
goals: Define and implement a tenant-mixer model that reproduces observed customer mixes (steady+spiky tenants)
Create a steady-state detector and golden-run fingerprinting mechanism to assert repeatable throughput
Integrate autoscaler policy emulator to test scale-up/down hysteresis and safety caps
Model admission/shaping at the fleet edge and verify graceful degradation and fair share across tenants
Produce an operator-facing runbook and a customer acceptance checklist with pass/fail criteria
acceptance_criteria: Galaxy harness can replay a saved tenant mix and produce a stable steady-state throughput signature across 3 independent runs (<=5% variance)
Measured p50/p90/p99 latencies and per-tenant throughput match golden-run within defined tolerances for three canonical mixes: enterprise-heavy, bursty-startups, mixed-saas
Autoscaler policy matrix tested: scale-up < 30s for sustained >80% GPU utilization, scale-down avoids oscillation for bursts < 60s
Fleet shaping test demonstrates admission-control fallbacks and documents per-tenant degradation order with reproducible traces
Customer Acceptance Test document drafted and validated with Solutions Engineering on two pilot customers
implementation_notes:
Harness components: traffic synthesizer (golang), tenant-mixer profile spec (yaml), steady-state detector (python),
measurement collector (prometheus + custom exporter), golden-run fingerprint store (S3)
Traffic shapes: steady, biexponential bursts, sinusoidal diurnal, microburst (1-5s), and long-tailed sessions
Autoscaler emulator: run the real policy code in a sandboxed controller against buffered telemetry to validate decisions
Admission control simulator: inject RSVP-like tokens at the front proxy to emulate shaping and preemption rules
KV cache warmup: include priming phase; report performance delta with/without warm caches to set realistic warmup windows
Golden-run fingerprint: aggregate series of p50/p90/p99, per-GPU throughput, per-tenant share, and a short trace sample (5s)
test_plan: Stage 1 — Calibration: collect representative traces from 3 production tenants and build tenant-mixer parametrizations
Stage 2 — Baseline runs: run Galaxy harness with empty cache, record ramp-to-steady and steady-state for 30m
Stage 3 — Warm-cache runs: run after priming sequence, verify improvements and update golden signature
Stage 4 — Autoscaler stress: create synthetic growth patterns to exercise scale-up & scale-down thresholds and observe overshoot/undershoot
Stage 5 — Fleet shaping: enable admission-control policies and assert per-tenant degradation ordering and fairness
Stage 6 — Customer Acceptance Tests: run two pilot customers' tenant-mix and produce CAT report for signoff

2026-03-07: Collected anonymized trace samples from pilot customers via data-collector v2; storage at s3://rwi-galaxy/traces/2026-03-07/
2026-03-11: Implemented steady-state detector and basic golden-run export; observed high variance for microburst-heavy mixes — investigating admission effects
2026-03-13: Autoscaler emulator integrated in sandbox; initial runs show oscillation when scale-down threshold < 60s — working on hysteresis tune set
risks: Access to representative production traces may be delayed by privacy review — mitigation: use synthetic parametrizations derived from public benchmarks
Autoscaler emulator behavior might diverge from production due to telemetry sampling differences — mitigation: run end-to-end test against a canary fleet
Customer mixes are diverse; a single set of golden signatures may not cover edge cases — mitigation: produce template signatures per industry archetype
next_steps: Finish admission-control simulator (eta 2026-03-18) and re-run microburst mixes
Lock down autoscaler hysteresis matrix and update default policy configs for Dedicated (eta 2026-03-21)
Draft Customer Acceptance Test (CAT) template and schedule two pilot runs with Solutions Eng
Prepare operator runbook with clear triage steps for observed variance >10% in golden runs
